resources.string: The downloader runs inside AutoSongs. Nothing else has to be installed.

AutoSongs itself is MIT licensed.

It includes LAME 3.100, an MP3 encoder, which is under the GNU Lesser General Public License 2.0. The Library and its use in this app are covered by that licence.

LAME is a separate library, so you are free to replace it with your own build - the licence allows that, and it allows you to modify this app for your own use and to reverse engineer it for debugging such modifications. The exact source of the version in this app is here:

https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/lame/lame/3.100/lame-3.100.tar.gz

and the script that builds it for Android is in the AutoSongs repository, in app/src/main/cpp/build-lame.sh.

The full licence text is inside the app, in assets/LICENSES/LAME-LGPL-2.0.txt. The notices for everything bundled are in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md in the repository.

The downloader is yt-dlp, which is in the public domain (The Unlicense).

Do them in this order — on some phones the second one is locked until the first is done.

If AutoSongs was installed from a file or a link rather than the Play Store, Android 13 and newer lock notification access until you turn on “Allow restricted settings”. It is in this page, under the ⋮ menu at the top right. Turning it on (and it may need “Update” tapped first) is what makes the switch below usable.
Notification access is needed so AutoSongs can see which track is playing.
Without this, Android may stop AutoSongs in the middle of a listening session. It is on the same app settings page, under Battery → Unrestricted.

On the app settings page: ⋮ → “Allow restricted settings” unlocks notification access, and Battery → “Unrestricted” keeps AutoSongs running. On some phones the battery setting is under “Special permissions” instead.
